The overall geometry of the gross Corrie fault-block structure is fairly well understood, from mapping of the currently-available 3D seismic data. However, the age of the reservoir unit is not known, due to a lack of both seismic resolution in that section (which could reveal the age of the section, and the real thickness pattern of that section downdip), and of any dating information from the discovery well. In addition, currently there is only an ODT from the well - pressure information is equivocal with regard to possible OWC levels. Finally, seismic control to the east is limited, and we need to acquire further data in the Norwegian sector to ascertain structural integrity and consequent volumetric estimates.
Main technical work required :
1. Broadband 3D seismic
2. Further studies - attempting to elucidate on the reservoir age and potential column height within the Corrie structure

Although the Bader structure is well delineated, further work is required to better understand the top seal and to position the exploration well and orientate the contingent inclined well to improve the chance of success and ensure maximum recovery of petroleum. 
The proposed 2 year Phase A work programme is designed to address these issues.
- reprocess the post stack 3D data to undertake detailed attribute analysis to further delineate the fault and fracture network within the structure, 
- studies to address the top seal risk will include using satellite imagery to detect possible oil seepage on the ocean surface, and 
- detailed sequence stratigraphic analysis of the top seal lithologies in the uppermost Cretaceous, Palaeocene and Eocene sections.

The Buzz Prospect has been mapped on the best possible dataset currently available over the area.  A 2 year Phase A work programme is planned to de-risk the remaining uncertainty by reprocessing part of the Rona Ridge (RR13) 3D survey. A gas discovery made by Texaco in 1977 in a simple rotated fault block north of the Claire field on the Rona Ridge. Until recently considered sub commercial in size. High quality Lower Cretaceous sandstone of 220ft gross and 200 feet net pay dry gas (97% methane). P50 or 2C contingent resources estimated at 154bcf recoverable from up to two development wells tied back via Laggan, Tormore or Claire pipeline infrastructure to the Shetlands Gas Plant (SGP). Minimal sub-surface risk as reservoir and hydrocarbons extent illuminated by 3D seismic in Core Development Area. Further upside exists in the Upside Area with up to 108bcf recoverable (P10 Prospective Resources). Corallian Energy Limited (Corallian) is applying for a Seaward Production Licence for Blocks 214/29b and 214/30c in the West of Shetland Basin, with the Innovate Licence Start Term being the Initial Term commencing in Phase A. The application is made in conjunction with a separate application made by Corallian to develop the Victory gas discovery in Block 207/1a.

The application for Victory contains a Straight to Second Term bid which if successful will result in new gas infrastructure for the area. Victory is considered by the applicants a commercially attractive sub-sea tie back opportunity which is stand-alone from a commercial viewpoint. However, development economic and operational synergies between for the two applications are considered of primary importance for the development of resources contained on Blocks 214/29b and 214/30c. Block 214/30c is located in approximately 550m water and contains the Laxford gas discovery, made in 1984 by British Gas well 214/30-1, which flowed 17.5 MMscfg / day from Palaeocene Vaila Sandstone. The discovery contains an estimated PMean recoverable gas resource of 81 billion cubic feet of gas and 1 million barrels of condensate (Corallian estimate). Block 214/29b contains the Scourie prospect, a Palaeocene Vaila Sandstone target exhibiting a seismic amplitude anomaly similar to that seen at the Glenlivet gas field located directly south of opportunity. key_work_comment: The trapping mechanism for this column is highly uncertain which results in the need for an improved seismic image to understand if the accumulation is a small attic pool or part of a larger contiguous Trap.   Furthermore, the developability of reservoir with poor properties is uncertain and an integrated study to understand as similar poor vertical results elsewhere have led to successful development (Skua).  Developability is also linked to fault throw magnitude and fault intensity which using the current seismic data set is difficult to estimate.  Bp estimate that faults with throws larger than 100 m can create compartments in this stratigraphy, thus disproving these or being able to design wells to mitigate them these will be critical to progressing the lead.

Success at the Genghis discovery maybe the enabler here.

Accurately assess remaining resources at Audrey; Decide whether appraisal drilling is required at Audrey and if so where an appraisal well would be located; If no appraisal well is required at Audrey, enable accurate subsurface mapping to proceed with field development planning;Accurately assess the range of in-place gas resources and exploration risk at Vampire North to enable a decision to be made regarding exploration drilling.
supplementary_information:

The key piece of technical work required for the maturation of Roseisle is the seismic reprocessing and interpretation of 1700km2 of 3D data, focusing on improved velocity modelling and migration (FWI and tomography) to de-risk the Lower Cretaceous reservoir model. Better resolution of faulting would be expected to further improve the structural interpretation.

Also key is the refinement of the existing basin model, including reassessing the sub-basin depth to the north of Roseisle, removal of intrusives from the Cretaceous thickness, and a detailed areal distribution of the Kimmeridge section. This should be integrated with an improved structural model, to improve the prediction of charge timing, development of overpressure and seal integrity.

Finally, a comprehensive review of shallow marine analogues and reservoir quality prediction is required.

Currently only the gross Flett fairway has been mapped rather than individual sand bodies and there is no single seismic dataset covering the whole prospect.

Seismic reprocessing will create a homogeneous dataset over the prospect which will allow more detailed mapping within the Flett fairway and additional geophysical analysis including AVO studies.

To mature the prospect the risk associated with the charge and migration and the seal must be reduced.

An improved basin model with a better understanding of the timing of charge in the area could improve the migration risk. Seismic reprocessing with a focus on the Eocene could improve the image leading to a better understanding of the injectite sands and hence an better understanding of the lateral seal with the Strachan Fan.

To mature the prospect the reservoir risk needs to be reduced. New seismic processing could improve the image of the Galloway structure and allow a seismic inversion to discriminate good quality reservoir presence from poor.

supplementary_information: Further information is provided in the APPENDIX B. The Vulcan gas field is located within the heart of IOG?s Central Hub Development (?Central Hub?). It is located approximately 7km southeast of Nailsworth, 10km northwest of Southwark with the Elland gas discovery located immediately to the east and the Battersea gas field 2km to the south. The Nailsworth gas field export route is conceptually planned above the field, located 1.5km west of the now decommissioned UR platform. Further technical work is required to establish the location of remaining gas in place, reservoir pressure and development well deliverability. However, a pre-conceptual  development well has been modelled to evaluate the commercial potential of redeveloping the field and achieving Maximum Economic Recovery.  Any development of the Vulcan field will be tied into infrastructure in the IOG Central Hub. The exact export route is to be determined; this could be direct into the platform designed for the Elland and Battersea development or direct into the Nailsworth to Southwark export pipeline.  IOG is currently undertaking the FEED study for the Nailsworth Development as the first part of the Central Hub. The FEED scope of work includes the preinvestment provision for the a tie-in on the Nailsworth to Southwark pipeline for a future re-development for the Battersea field, which could also tie in the Vulcan field.
additional_information: Any redevelopment of the field will require compression as the modelled reservoir pressure is between 1000-1500psi. As part of IOG?s JV Hub Strategy, compression at the SBRF is planned to be installed and operational by Q1 2027, with ongoing work to establish how this can be accelerated. Any re-development of the Vulcan field must be made after compression has been installed.

supplementary_information: Although this application is for a Phase A entry (due to reasons mentioned in Additional information), the prospect is considered attractive, drill-ready and some high level well planning and engineering work has been carried out. The exploration well would be drilled to target a Minimum Economic Volume at the Pentland and Skagerrak stratigraphic levels, while tagging the updip portion of the Fulmar target. In the case of encountering hydrocarbon-bearing sands at the Fulmar target level, the well would likely be side-tracked to chase a downdip contact and prove an economic volume. A preliminary well trajectory has been chosen to remain vertical in the Palaeocene section and build to an angle of ~20 degrees in the chalk and through the Jurassic/Triassic target intervals. This trajectory is optimal for testing economic volumes in both the Pentland and Skagerrak intervals, while avoiding the depleted Forties sandstones of the Scoter field as far as possible. A Level 0 dry hole well cost estimate of ú64 mln (100% cost) has been estimated for a four-string well design with contingent 11 3/4 liner.
additional_information: The Scoter Deep prospect is HPHT and straddles Block 22/30a (Shell-operated Scoter FDA, P012 licence), Block 23/26d (Harbour-operated Scoter FDA, P264 licence) and Block 23/26c (open acreage, this application). The Scoter field has now ceased production and a decommissioning programme was submitted to the NSTA in August 2022. The optimal well location to test the prospect at all three stratigraphic target levels is within the Harbour-operated P264 licence, which also contains a significant portion of the P90-P50 volumes. Shell would therefore need access to this acreage, in addition to Block 23/26c, to be able to make a firm well commitment on the prospect.

key_work_comment: No further technical work required (drill-ready prospect).
supplementary_information: Although this application is for a Phase A entry, the prospect is considered attractive, drill-ready and some high level well planning work has been carried out. The exploration well would be drilled to target the Upper Jurassic Heather and Fulmar and the Middle Jurassic Pentland stratigraphic levels in an optimal position and avoid leaving an attic volume up dip, the well will be planned to tag the down dip part of the Joanne reservoir. In the case of encountering hydrocarbon-bearing sands in any of the Jurassic target levels and good reservoir quality sands in the Joanne, the well would likely be side-tracked up dip to test the Joanne level and prove an economic volume. A preliminary well trajectory has been chosen to remain vertical in the Palaeocene section, beginning to build angle at approx. 11500 ft, below the Stella field reservoirs (Andrew and Ekofisk) which are likely to be depleted. In the preliminary design an angle of ~12 degrees in the chalk and through the Jurassic/Triassic target intervals has been adopted. This trajectory is optimal for testing economic volumes in the Heather, Fulmar and Pentland intervals, while avoiding the depleted Andrew sandstones and Ekofisk chalk reservoirs of the Stella field as much as possible. A Level 1 dry hole well cost estimate of ú67.5 mln (100 % cost, including site survey costs, and share of mobilisation/demobilisation costs in a multi-well campaign) has been estimated for a five-string well design with contingent 7 liner. Additional well planning will be required, including a site survey and shallow hazard screening, to refine the well design.
additional_information: The crest of the structure lies in Block 30/6a: stratigraphically split into pre-Chalk (50 % Shell U.K. Limited and 50% NEO Energy) and post-Chalk (operated by Ithaca, producing from the Palaeogene Andrew and Ekofisk  reservoirs of the Stella field). An exploration well would likely be drilled within 30/6a, requiring a drill through agreement with the shallow partnership. In volumetric cases greater than the P90 contact, volumes would extend into block 30/6c and a further appraisal well may be required in 30/6c. Shell U.K. Limited are the proposed operator and licence administrator with a proposed equity split in block 30/6c of 55.5 % (Shell U.K. Limited) and 45.5 % (NEO Energy). The Joelle prospect is HPHT.

In the case of encountering hydrocarbon-bearing sands in any of the Jurassic target levels and good reservoir quality sands in the Joanne, the well would likely be side-tracked up dip to test the Joanne level and prove an economic volume. A preliminary well trajectory has been chosen to remain vertical in the Palaeocene section, beginning to build angle at approx. 11500 ft, below the Stella field reservoirs (Andrew and Ekofisk) which are likely to be depleted. In the preliminary design an angle of ~12 degrees in the chalk and through the Jurassic/Triassic target intervals has been adopted. This trajectory is optimal for testing economic volumes in the Heather, Fulmar and Pentland intervals, while avoiding the depleted Andrew sandstones and Ekofisk chalk reservoirs of the Stella field as much as possible. A Level 1 dry hole well cost estimate of ú67.5 mln (100 % cost, including site survey costs, and share of mobilisation/demobilisation costs in a multi-well campaign) has been estimated for a five-string well design with contingent 7 liner. Additional well planning will be required, including a site survey and shallow hazard screening, to refine the well design.
additional_information: The crest of the structure lies in Block 30/6a: stratigraphically split into pre-Chalk (50 % Shell U.K. Limited and 50% NEO Energy) and post-Chalk (operated by Ithaca, producing from the Palaeogene Andrew and Ekofisk  reservoirs of the Stella field). An exploration well would likely be drilled within 30/6a, requiring a drill through agreement with the shallow partnership. In volumetric cases greater than the P90 contact, volumes would extend into block 30/6c and a further appraisal well may be required in 30/6c. Shell U.K. Limited are the proposed operator and licence administrator with a proposed equity split in block 30/6c of 55.5 % (Shell U.K. Limited) and 45.5 % (NEO Energy). The Joelle prospect is HPHT.
